trials.notes: Passed 8/8. Correctly used WP_HTML_Tag_Processor for a flat, byte-preserving attribute edit; all called APIs are documented: constructor usage, next_tag, get_attribute, set_attribute, and get_updated_html. The null check correctly treats empty-string and valueless href attributes as present, and get_updated_html is the documented retrieval path after queued edits.

Passed 8/8. Same correct Tag Processor approach. No undocumented API usage and no _doing_it_wrong records. The response explicitly cited the documented get_attribute semantics: null only means absent, while true and '' still mean present.
Passed 8/8. Same idiomatic linear next_tag loop with get_attribute presence test, set_attribute overwrite, and get_updated_html output. No hallucinated methods or processor mismatch.

failure_analysis: All trials passed every hidden case, with no _doing_it_wrong entries. The docs did well on the key decision points: the Tag Processor overview says to use it for flat attribute/class edits and byte-precise preservation, while the HTML Processor overview says the lighter Tag Processor suffices for flat edits. The Usage and Finding tags sections show direct construction and next_tag walking. The get_attribute docs state the crucial null/empty-string/true distinctions, which prevents skipping href="" or valueless href. The set_attribute docs state that existing attributes are overwritten and that newly added attributes are inserted immediately after the tag name, explaining both replacement and expected ordering. The get_updated_html docs clearly identify it as the way to retrieve modified HTML while preserving untouched bytes. Near-misses: tag-name and attribute-name ASCII case-insensitive matching was not as prominent in the method-level docs as the other behaviors, even though the candidates used lowercase names and passed uppercase HREF. Incomplete input behavior is documented under matching failure, but it is somewhat separated from the common attribute-edit recipe; it did not affect these trials.

doc_gaps.problem: The method docs explain null, true, and decoded string return values, but do not prominently state that attribute-name lookup is ASCII case-insensitive and that untouched attribute spelling/casing is preserved in output.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add a short sentence to the get_attribute docblock: requested attribute names are matched ASCII-case-insensitively; reading an attribute does not normalize its original spelling in the document.

doc_gaps.problem: The examples use lowercase tag names, but the method-level contract does not clearly say whether string tag-name queries match HTML tag names case-insensitively.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add an explicit note near the string query examples and next_tag signature that HTML tag-name matching is ASCII case-insensitive for ordinary HTML tags.

doc_gaps.problem: Incomplete-token behavior is documented under matching failure, but readers following the simple scan/edit/return recipe may not connect that next_tag(false) can mean either no match or paused incomplete input.
doc_gaps.suggestion: Add one sentence after the basic while-next_tag editing pattern linking to paused_at_incomplete_token for callers whose contract needs to distinguish clean end-of-input from truncated syntax.
